# Benchmarks

*Generated by `scripts/gen_bench_pages.py` from the `oml-bench/1` results in `eval/bench/results/`; do not edit by hand. Regenerate with `python scripts/gen_bench_pages.py`, and CI fails when this page differs from what it writes.*

**Default search pipeline:** `bm25` (the deployment's `search.default` when unset; [configuration](../../operations/configuration.md)). How the default is chosen: ADR-0049 d9, and the measurements behind it in [the benchmark report](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/eval/bench/REPORT.md).

Every number below went through the served path: memories written over HTTP by an agent key, promoted by reviewer keys of other principals, and recalled through `oml_read` over `/mcp`, one query at a time. Reference rows are offline and have no latency. Latency is the client's wall time per call, in milliseconds.

**The latency ceiling.** Under row security no text index serves a recall: `@@`, `%` and `ts_rank` are not leakproof (ADR-0034 d13), so every pipeline reads the stored lexemes of every row the key may read, and its cost grows with those rows. Storing the lexemes made a row several times cheaper, not free: the scale lane measured an every-word match over a stored `simple` vector past 50 ms near 70,000 readable rows (`bench/scale/REPORT.md` on `feat/scale-bench`), and `bm25` reads more per row than that match, so on abstract-length text it crosses the line far sooner, as the tables show. Latency at scale is not solved by stored lexemes.

## [Synthetic recall set](recall-synthetic.md)

200 memories, 121 queries. Measured 2026-11-05 on commit `2b0cf53`, `71b7b69`; build release, host 8 vCPU / 15 GB, postgres 17.9; build release, host 8 vCPU / 15 GB, postgres 18.6.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| keyword-all | 121 | 0.156 | 0.174 | – | 0.826 | 14.2 | 18.6 |
| keyword-any | 121 | 0.689 | 0.843 | – | 0.033 | 18.9 | 29.7 |
| bm25 | 121 | 0.876 | 0.926 | – | 0.000 | 16.3 | 21.2 |
| bm25-trigram | 121 | 0.874 | 0.950 | – | 0.000 | 30.4 | 41.9 |
| bm25-rerank | 121 | 0.906 | 0.950 | – | 0.000 | 356 | 487 |
